description: A study of cash crop production in Tanzania, covering major cash crops and their growing areas, ecological requirements, husbandry, processing, marketing, and the problems facing the sub-sector and their solutions.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best defines a cash crop?

options.text: A crop grown mainly to be sold for income rather than for direct consumption by the grower
A crop grown only to feed the farmer's own family
Any crop that grows during the rainy season
A crop that is grown without using any fertiliser

mcq.explanation: A cash crop is grown primarily for sale to earn money, unlike a food crop which is grown mainly for the farmer's own consumption.

mcq.questionText: In which region of Tanzania is Arabica coffee most associated with the slopes of a tall mountain?
mcq.explanation: Arabica coffee is grown on the cool, high-altitude slopes of Mount Kilimanjaro, as well as in Mbeya and Kagera.

mcq.questionText: Cotton in Tanzania is grown mainly in which of the following zones?

options.text: The Lake Zone, especially Mwanza and Shinyanga

mcq.explanation: Cotton is the leading cash crop of the Lake Zone, particularly Mwanza, Shinyanga, Mara and Simiyu.

mcq.questionText: Which cash crop is Zanzibar historically most famous for producing?
mcq.explanation: Zanzibar (especially Pemba) is world-renowned for clove production, which has long been a major export.

mcq.questionText: Cashew nut production in Tanzania is concentrated mainly in which regions?
mcq.explanation: The Southern coastal regions of Mtwara and Lindi are the leading cashew nut producing areas of Tanzania.

mcq.questionText: Tea in Tanzania thrives best under which ecological condition?

options.text: Hot, dry lowlands with little rainfall
Cool, high-altitude areas with high, well-distributed rainfall such as Mufindi and Njombe

mcq.explanation: Tea requires cool temperatures, high altitude and abundant, evenly distributed rainfall, conditions found in Mufindi, Njombe and Bukoba.

mcq.questionText: Which crop is the main cash crop of the Tabora region?
mcq.explanation: Tabora is the leading tobacco-growing region in Tanzania, mainly producing flue-cured Virginia tobacco.

mcq.questionText: Pyrethrum is valued chiefly because it is used to produce which product?
mcq.explanation: Pyrethrum flowers contain pyrethrins used to make natural, environmentally friendly insecticides; it is grown in cool highlands such as Mbeya and Iringa.

mcq.questionText: Sisal is grown mainly for which purpose?

options.text: Production of hard fibre used in ropes, twine and sacks

mcq.explanation: Sisal is a fibre crop; its leaves are processed (decorticated) to extract hard fibre used for ropes, twine, carpets and sacks.

options.text: By seeds sown directly in the field
By bulbils and suckers obtained from the mother plant

mcq.explanation: Sisal is propagated vegetatively using bulbils (formed on the flower pole) and suckers raised in a nursery before transplanting.

mcq.questionText: The process of extracting sisal fibre from the leaves is called:
mcq.explanation: Decortication is the mechanical crushing and scraping of sisal leaves to separate the fibre from the pulp.

mcq.questionText: The process of separating cotton lint from its seeds is known as:
mcq.explanation: Ginning is carried out in ginneries to separate the cotton lint (fibre) from the seeds after harvesting seed cotton.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a major problem facing cash crop production in Tanzania?

options.text: Excessive use of modern machinery by all farmers
Fluctuating and often low world market prices for crops
Too much capital available to farmers

mcq.explanation: Unstable and low world prices reduce farmers' incomes and discourage production; other problems include pests, poor inputs and weak markets.

mcq.questionText: Which statement correctly distinguishes cash crops from food crops?

options.text: Cash crops are grown mainly for sale while food crops are grown mainly for consumption
Cash crops are always perennial while food crops are always annual
Cash crops never need fertiliser while food crops always do
Cash crops are grown only by women while food crops are grown by men

mcq.explanation: The key difference is purpose: cash crops earn income through sale, while food crops mainly feed the household, though a surplus food crop may also be sold.

mcq.questionText: Coffee berries are best harvested when they:

options.text: Have dried and fallen to the ground

mcq.explanation: Ripe coffee cherries are red and are selectively hand-picked; picking unripe green berries lowers quality.

fib.questionText: A crop grown mainly for sale to earn income is called a _____ crop.
fib.explanation: A cash crop is produced primarily for sale rather than for the grower's own consumption.

fib.questionText: Arabica coffee is grown on the cool slopes of Mount _____ in northern Tanzania.
fib.explanation: The high-altitude slopes of Mount Kilimanjaro provide the cool conditions Arabica coffee needs.

fib.questionText: The Lake Zone regions of Mwanza and _____ are the leading cotton-producing areas of Tanzania.
fib.explanation: Mwanza and Shinyanga, in the Lake Zone, dominate Tanzania's cotton production.

fib.questionText: The separation of cotton lint from its seeds is called _____.
fib.explanation: Ginning is done in ginneries to obtain clean cotton lint from seed cotton.

fib.questionText: Extraction of fibre from sisal leaves is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Decortication mechanically scrapes the pulp away to leave the sisal fibre.

fib.questionText: The region of Tanzania most famous for tobacco production is _____.
fib.explanation: Tabora is the leading tobacco-growing region, mainly producing flue-cured Virginia tobacco.

fib.questionText: Cashew nuts are grown mainly in the southern coastal regions of Mtwara and _____.
fib.explanation: Mtwara and Lindi are the principal cashew nut producing regions of Tanzania.

fib.questionText: The island of _____ is world-famous for the production of cloves.
fib.explanation: Zanzibar, especially Pemba island, is historically the leading clove producer.

fib.questionText: Tea is grown in the cool highland areas of Mufindi and _____ in the Southern Highlands.
fib.explanation: Mufindi and Njombe have the high altitude and rainfall suited to tea growing.

fib.questionText: Pyrethrum flowers are processed to make natural _____ used to kill pests.
fib.explanation: The pyrethrins in pyrethrum flowers are used to manufacture natural insecticides.

tf.questionText: Cash crops are grown mainly for sale to earn income.
tf.explanation: By definition, cash crops are produced primarily for sale rather than home consumption.

tf.questionText: Cotton in Tanzania is grown mainly on the slopes of Mount Kilimanjaro.
tf.explanation: Cotton is grown mainly in the Lake Zone (Mwanza, Shinyanga); Mount Kilimanjaro is associated with Arabica coffee.

tf.questionText: Cloves are a major cash crop of Zanzibar.
tf.explanation: Zanzibar, particularly Pemba, has long been a leading world producer of cloves.

tf.questionText: Tea grows best in hot, dry lowland areas with little rainfall.
tf.explanation: Tea requires cool, high-altitude areas with high and well-distributed rainfall, such as Mufindi and Njombe.

tf.questionText: Ginning is the process of separating cotton lint from the seeds.
tf.explanation: Ginning, done in ginneries, removes the seeds to obtain clean cotton lint.

tf.questionText: Sisal is propagated by sowing seeds directly into the field.
tf.explanation: Sisal is propagated vegetatively using bulbils and suckers raised in a nursery, not by direct seed sowing.

tf.questionText: Cashew nut production in Tanzania is concentrated in the Mtwara and Lindi regions.
tf.explanation: The southern coastal regions of Mtwara and Lindi are the main cashew nut producing areas.

tf.questionText: Fluctuating world market prices are one of the problems facing cash crop production in Tanzania.
tf.explanation: Unstable and often low prices reduce farmers' incomes and discourage cash crop production.

tf.questionText: Pyrethrum is grown mainly to produce cooking oil.
tf.explanation: Pyrethrum is grown for its flowers, which yield pyrethrins used to make natural insecticides, not cooking oil.

tf.questionText: Ripe coffee cherries are red and are selectively picked to maintain good quality.
tf.explanation: Selective hand-picking of red, ripe cherries ensures high-quality coffee.

summary.correctAnswer: A cash crop is a crop grown mainly for sale to earn income rather than for the grower's own consumption.
summary.explanation: The defining feature is that it is produced primarily for the market.

summary.questionText: State the main difference between a cash crop and a food crop.
summary.correctAnswer: A cash crop is grown mainly for sale to earn money, while a food crop is grown mainly to provide food for the farmer's household.
summary.explanation: The distinction is based on the main purpose of growing the crop.

summary.questionText: Give two examples of major cash crops grown in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Examples include coffee, cotton, sisal, tea, cashew nuts, tobacco, pyrethrum, cloves and sugarcane.
summary.explanation: These are the leading export and cash crops of Tanzania.

summary.questionText: Name the regions where coffee is grown in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Coffee is grown in Kilimanjaro, Mbeya and Kagera.
summary.explanation: Arabica grows on cool highlands (Kilimanjaro, Mbeya) while Robusta is common in Kagera.

summary.questionText: State two importances of cash crops to the national economy.
summary.correctAnswer: Cash crops earn foreign exchange through exports and provide raw materials for local industries; they also create employment and government revenue.
summary.explanation: Cash crops are a major source of export earnings and support agro-industries and jobs.

summary.questionText: State two importances of cash crops to the individual farmer.
summary.correctAnswer: Cash crops provide income to meet family needs such as school fees, food, clothing and medical care, and improve the farmer's standard of living.
summary.explanation: The income earned helps farmers meet household needs and invest in farming.

summary.questionText: State the ecological requirements for growing tea.
summary.correctAnswer: Tea requires cool temperatures, high altitude, high and well-distributed rainfall, and deep, well-drained acidic soils.
summary.explanation: Such conditions are found in Mufindi, Njombe and Bukoba.

summary.questionText: Briefly describe the processing of cotton after harvesting.
summary.correctAnswer: Seed cotton is taken to a ginnery where ginning separates the lint (fibre) from the seeds; the lint is then baled for sale while seeds are used for oil and seed.
summary.explanation: Ginning is the key processing step that yields marketable cotton lint.

summary.questionText: State three problems facing cash crop production in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Problems include fluctuating and low world prices, pests and diseases, shortage of capital and inputs, poor transport and storage, and unreliable rainfall.
summary.explanation: These factors lower yields, quality and farmers' incomes.

summary.questionText: Suggest three solutions to the problems facing cash crop production in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Solutions include providing stable markets and fair prices through cooperatives, supplying improved inputs and credit, controlling pests and diseases, improving transport and processing, and giving farmers extension education.
summary.explanation: Such measures raise production, quality and farmers' incomes.

hoq.questionText: A farmer in Mtwara harvests cashew nuts but earns very little despite a good crop. Which combination of factors most likely explains the low income?

options.text: Low and fluctuating world prices together with sale of raw nuts and high transport costs
Excellent road network and guaranteed high export prices
Abundant cheap credit and on-farm processing facilities
Strong cooperative marketing with stable contract prices

hoq.explanation: Low world prices, selling unprocessed raw nuts (which fetch less than kernels) and high transport costs all reduce the farmer's net income; the other options describe favourable conditions.

hoq.questionText: Why is selective hand-picking of red, ripe cherries important in coffee production, and what is the main consequence of picking unripe berries?

options.text: It saves labour, and unripe berries improve flavour
It ensures uniform high quality, while unripe berries lower the grade and price of the coffee
It speeds drying, and unripe berries are easier to pulp
It reduces pests, and unripe berries raise the bean weight

hoq.explanation: Only ripe red cherries give good-quality beans; mixing in unripe berries lowers the grade and therefore the price farmers receive.

hoq.questionText: A region has cool temperatures, high altitude and high, well-distributed rainfall on deep, well-drained soils. Which cash crop would be most suitable, and why?

options.text: Cashew nut, because it needs cool wet highlands
Cotton, because it requires high rainfall throughout the year
Tea, because it thrives in cool, high-altitude areas with abundant, well-distributed rainfall
Sisal, because it grows only in cold wet conditions

hoq.explanation: Tea matches these ecological conditions, which is why it is grown in cool highlands such as Mufindi and Njombe; cashew and cotton prefer warmer drier areas and sisal tolerates dry conditions.
